item.title: Micro‐Scale Mapping of Oviposition Activity Using UAV ‐Derived Microenvironment Structure: A Case Study of Aedes albopictus
item.description:
Keyi Yu, Zijun Zhou, Yibin Zhou, Jianping Wu, Shenjun Yao
Transactions in GIS, vol. 30, issue 7
DOI: 10.1111/tgis.70473
ABSTRACT Fine‐scale oviposition hotspots can be obscured by coarse environmental representations. We evaluated whether UAV‐derived microenvironment structure adds information beyond proximity‐based and Sentinel‐2 representations for mapping Aedes albopictus oviposition hotspots. Using 282 monitoring sites on a Shanghai university campus, we compared Baseline, Sentinel‐2, and UAV predictor configurations with XGBoost and Random Forest under repeated stratified cross‐validation. With XGBoost, the UAV model achieved higher Accuracy (0.80) and Cohen's κ (0.34) than both comparison models, while Sentinel‐2 achieved slightly higher Recall (0.47 vs. 0.42); UAV AUC was 0.64. Under the same 57‐site inspection quota, Precision@20% increased from 0.33 for both comparison models to 0.49 with UAV variables, an approximately 48% relative improvement. SHAP identified fine‐scale land‐cover and structural variables as important predictive contributors. Although overall discrimination remained moderate, UAV‐derived structural information improved fixed‐quota hotspot prioritization, supporting its use as a fine‐scale follow‐up tool in preselected high‐priority areas.

item.title: Detecting Intercity Mobility Subsystems via an Ordered Stochastic Block Model and Anisotropic Metrics: Evidence From China's Pre‐Spring Festival Period
item.description:
Jianfa Shen, Jun Chu, Hengyu Gu, Haoyu Hu, Junwei Zhang
Transactions in GIS, vol. 30, issue 7
DOI: 10.1111/tgis.70469
ABSTRACT While directed networks are a focal point in intercity mobility research, there are limited studies quantifying the uncertainty of directionality using network and geometric indicators. To address this limitation, this study proposes a framework using an ordered stochastic block model with a sequential analytical workflow of anisotropic metrics to analyze intercity mobility before China's Spring Festival. Our findings indicate that China's Spring Festival return‐mobility consists of three subsystems with ordered subgroups. Asymmetric intercity flows establish a hierarchical structure, with developed regions positioned at the top and labor‐exporting cities at the bottom. Flows in the South and East China subsystems are predominantly oriented toward the northwest and west‐northwest, respectively, consistent with return migration to inland hometowns. The results demonstrate the efficacy of combining network science with geometric directionality in characterizing complex spatial interactions, offering valuable insights for urban and regional planning.
